the elucidation of the molecular basis of oxidative damage and the elucidation of mechanisms of the prevention of errors caused by the oxidative damage.
the identification of mammalian MutT proteins and the determination of the molecular mechanisms of their action.
the elucidation of the molecular basis for the repair mechanism against transcriptional errors caused oxidative damage.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both NUDTs and MTH1 prevent translational errors due to oxidative damage by eliminating 8-oxoguanine containing ribonucleotidetriphosphate from precursor pool.
the mammalian MutT-related proteins NUDT5 (and probably MTH1) prevent translational errors by degrading the 8-oxoguanine-containing ribonucleotide precursors.

the human MutT-related proteins NUDT5 (hMTH1 homologous protein) and MTH1 (8-oxoguanine triphosphatase) are involved in preventing translational errors caused not only by 8-oxoguanylating agents but also by oxidative damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human MTH1 gene product is a novel protein which has an important role in preventing transcriptional errors in cells.

NUDT5 is the main enzyme to prevent the misincorporations of 8-oxidized guanines into the mRNA, whereas MTH1 has an additional activity to prevent the mispairing of 8-oxide guanine with adenine in DNA.
NUDT5 is a specific 8-oxoguanine nucleotide triphosphatase and MTH1 is an 8-oxodinucleotide triphosphodiesterase.
The main takeaway from our work is that
NUDT5 is a novel human enzyme for preventing oxidative damage of proteins.
MTH1 and NUDT5 play an important role in the prevention of the accumulation of erroneous proteins by eliminating the oxidized ribonucleotidase from the RNA pool in human cells.
NUDT5 is a novel enzyme that can prevent translational errors in human cells.
